item: Baltic birch plywood 18 mm, 5 x 5 ft sheet (B/BB)
for a pair: 3 sheets (4 if the gables are birch and you want a spare)
source: Cherokee Wood, The Wood & Shop, Rockler, MakerStock, local plywood dealer
note: 3 sheets cover both cabinets and both gable glue-ups (fab/out/dxf/sheets.svg). Measure the real thickness before CNC work.

item: CNC cutting of the panels (2D profiles, two 3 mm groove pockets, one 1.5 mm pocket)
source: local CNC cabinet or sign shop; makerspace ShopBot; SpeakerHardware custom shop (8-12 weeks)
note: No instant online service cuts 18 mm plywood (SendCutSend stops at 12 mm).

item: Gable, route A: CNC-milled laminated birch block (two halves, 3-axis)
source: local CNC sign, millwork or pattern shop; JMP Wood (NY/NJ)
note: fab/out/step/gable-block-lower.step and -upper.step

item: Gable, route B: 3D-printed in four pieces (PETG or ASA), filled and painted
note: fab/out/stl/gable-print/. A material change from the spec's solid birch: the owner's call.

item: Wood glue (Titebond II or III)
Dowels 10 mm x 40 mm (block to body)
Glue blocks or brad nails (optional)
Bowl test slice (PLA is fine), 250 x 240 x 150
source: makerspace; Craftcloud; JLC3DP (40% US tariff on plastics)
note: fab/out/stl/gable-test-slice.stl or the -lower/-upper pair for support-free printing

item: Port: tube with flange + flare collar (PETG or ASA, not PLA)
note: Print the tube 10 mm long and trim to tune at 32 Hz

item: Woofer: Dayton Audio DSA315-8 (12 in)
note: Shortlisted for every tier. DS315-8 ($149.99) is the non-metal alternative.

item: Midrange: SB Acoustics SB17MFC35-8 (budget/mid) or Satori MR16P-8 (premium)
Tweeter: Scan-Speak Illuminator R3004/602200 (mid/premium) or Peerless OC25SC65-04 in a printed ring (budget)
note: Faceplate 62 mm max: the throat is 66

item: Binding posts, pair (4 mm banana, about 64 mm spacing)
note: Re-cut the plate's 10 mm holes to the posts bought

item: Crossover parts (air-core inductors, film capacitors, resistors, boards)
note: Designed from measurements in VituixCAD or XSim; low-DCR woofer inductor

item: Internal wire, 14-16 AWG, and spade/crimp terminals
Measurement kit: miniDSP UMIK-1 mic + Dayton DATS V3 + REW (free)
note: Needed on every crossover route

item: Optional DSP audition: miniDSP 2x4 HD + three amp channels per speaker
note: Lets you hear and tune the crossover before building it passive

item: Acoustic damping (polyfill or wool, felt for the bowl's faceplate gap)
note: Loosely fill the mid chamber; line the woofer chamber walls

item: Gasket tape for drivers, putty to seal the wire holes
note: The tweeter pocket's wire hole must be sealed or it leaks the woofer box

item: Cast-letter wordmark, 3.18 mm (0.125 in) sheet, laser cut: brass, aluminium or stainless
for a pair: 4 sets (front and back of each speaker)
unit price USD: ~$39 order minimum; letters a few dollars each
source: SendCutSend; OSHCut or Xometry for the i-dot and for bronze
note: fab/out/metal/wordmark-letters.dxf. The renders show silver letters: stainless or aluminium, polished; brass if the owner wants them warm.

item: Bronze or brass Nutrition Facts plate, 318 x 312 x 3, R3, etched and paint-filled
source: Woodland Manufacturing, Impact Signs, Saifee Signs; or a blank + local fiber-laser engraver
note: fab/out/metal/plate-facts.svg. Hold the order until the speaker is measured: the plate states 91 dB.

item: Terminal plate 128 x 64 x 3 (aluminium 5052 or brass)
note: fab/out/metal/terminal-plate.dxf

item: Letter mounting: epoxy (3M DP420 or Devcon), optional 1/16 in brass rod pins
note: Templates: fab/out/metal/wordmark-template-front.pdf and -back.pdf

source: local sign shop, CraftCuts, or a library Cricut
note: fab/out/marks/*.svg. Paint the text colour first, mask the letters, paint the field, peel.
